newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Kohl supports Slovenia's NATO bid.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Kohl supports Slovenia's NATO bid.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl told Slovenia's Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek on Wednesday that Germany supported the ex-Yugoslav republic's bid to join NATO and the European Union.

Government spokesman Peter Hausmann said Kohl had made it clear the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation was still open to new members after last week's alliance summit in Madrid invited Poland, Hungary and the Czech republic to join.

Slovenia and Romania had hoped they might also be included in the first wave of NATO enlargement, but after only the three favourites were invited in alliance leaders said last week the two countries would be considered in future rounds.
"The chancellor stressed Germany's emphatic support for Slovenia's membership of the EU," Hausmann said in a statement.

"He also said the German government had great sympathy for Slovenia's wish to join NATO soon and supports Slovenia in its efforts. The NATO summit in Madrid made it clear the alliance is open to more new members," the statement said.
Slovenia ratified its association agreement with the European Union on Tuesday in a parliamentary vote coinciding with Brussels' decision to invite the country to begin full entry talks.
